questions.q: What kind of work does the Silver layer primarily apply to bronze's output?
options: Casting, deduplication, and null handling — exactly the PySpark techniques from Foundations' Chapter 4
Business-level aggregation for dashboards
Nothing — silver is identical to bronze
Only schema-level renaming, with no actual data cleaning
questions.explain: Silver is where all of that PySpark work actually gets used, for real, on real ingested data.

questions.q: Why does casting a column's type need to happen before deduplicating on it?
options: dropDuplicates on a string "14.50" and a double 14.5 would treat them as different values, since they aren't even the same type yet
Deduplication only works on already-deduplicated data
Casting is not actually required before deduplication
PySpark automatically casts types before every dropDuplicates call
questions.explain: Cast, then dedupe, then handle nulls — roughly this order, every time, for exactly this reason.

questions.q: What does "conforming" data mean in the silver layer?
options: Making data consistent with a shared standard — same column names, units, and categorical values — across potentially multiple source systems
Converting all data to a single file format
Removing every column not needed by gold
Encrypting sensitive columns before they reach silver
questions.explain: If two sources name the same field differently, silver is where that gets reconciled so gold never has to know.

questions.q: What is the basic mechanical shape of a layer transition in medallion architecture?
options: Read from the previous layer's table, transform it, and write to a new named table for the current layer
Directly modify the previous layer's table in place
Copy the previous layer's files without reading them as a DataFrame
Always start from a fresh CSV file rather than the previous layer
questions.explain: This exact pattern — spark.table() in, transform, saveAsTable() out — repeats at every layer transition.

questions.q: Is any of the syntax used to build silver genuinely new material, beyond what Foundations covered?
options: No — casting, deduplication, and null handling are all exactly the techniques from Foundations Lessons 48, 51, and 52
Yes, silver requires an entirely new set of PySpark functions
Yes, silver can only be built using SQL, never the DataFrame API
Yes, silver requires Unity Catalog to be enabled first
questions.explain: Silver is exactly where that earlier PySpark material gets put to real use, on real ingested data.
